content: 1. Adverse effects such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, and menorrhagia may occur. These should be monitored closely. 2. Fostemsavir can increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Co-administration should be avoided if possible, or the dose of the BCRP substrate should be modified. The ethinyl estradiol dose should not exceed 30 mcg/day. 3. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of frovatriptan by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, and close monitoring is recommended. 4. Gemifloxacin can decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. 5. Ferrous fumarate decreases gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be considered, and close monitoring is advised. 6. Grapefruit can increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Ethinyl estradiol increases green tea levels by decreasing its elimination. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 8. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 9. Gymnema decreases ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 10. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of hemin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may also decrease hemin effects. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 11. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of heparin by pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of hyaluronidase. Estrogens in large systemic doses may render tissues partially resistant to hyaluronidase, requiring larger amounts of the enzyme for equivalent dispersing effects. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Ferrous fumarate decreases ibandronate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases ferrous fumarate levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 15. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 16. Iloperidone increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, potentially increasing plasma levels of drugs eliminated by CYP3A4. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 17. Ethinyl estradiol may increase serum concentrations of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) like imipramine by decreasing oxidative metabolism. This may lead to increased TCA adverse effects. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Indinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 19. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin aspart, insulin degludec, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, insulin lispro, and regular human insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 20. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 21. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 22. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors like itraconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 24. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Ethinyl estradiol decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Plasma concentrations of lamotrigine may be significantly reduced. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 26. Lansoprazole decreases ferrous fumarate levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 28. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 30. Leniolisib increases systemic exposure of BCRP substrates, including ethinyl estradiol. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 31. Lesinurad decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used, as hormonal contraceptives alone may not be reliable. 32. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of letrozole by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Letrozole should not be given concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 33. Ferrous fumarate decreases levodopa levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral administration of iron salts should be separated from levodopa by at least two hours. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 34. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. 35. Ferrous fumarate decreases levofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 36. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 37. Ferrous fumarate decreases levothyroxine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral administration of these agents should be separated by four hours. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 38. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of liraglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 39. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least one hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. 40. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of lomitapide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 41. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the lonafarnib dose and monitor closely for arrhythmias and other events. 42. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of lonapegsomatropin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may reduce serum insulin-like growth factor-1 response to lonapegsomatropin. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended.
